articles.title: Neuroimaging study links heightened sensitivity to peer rejection with harsher parenting after childhood abuse
articles.summary: Why does childhood abuse carry over into harsh parenting in some families but not others? New fMRI findings indicate the connection holds only when a mother's brain reacts more strongly to negative than positive social feedback.

articles.title: Reanalysis of 1950s LSD experiments challenges the idea that psychedelics make art more creative
articles.summary: A reanalysis of 140 paintings from Oscar Janiger’s mid-century LSD studies found that professional artists painted more abstractly under the drug, while blind expert ratings showed no gains in creativity or aesthetic appeal.

articles.title: Common classroom accommodations for ADHD fail to improve student behavior or schoolwork in clinical trial
articles.summary: In a clinical trial of elementary students with ADHD, extra time, frequent breaks, standing desks, and low-distraction workspaces failed to improve behavior or schoolwork. Meanwhile, structured behavioral supports and stimulant medication substantially reduced classroom rule-breaking.

articles.title: Why stopping SSRIs can cause anxiety: A rebound in serotonin neuron activity may play a role
articles.summary: Stopping an SSRI may release serotonin neurons from the restraint they experience during treatment, triggering a rebound in activity. A mouse study links this rebound, along with hippocampal activation, to anxiety after discontinuation.

articles.title: Ozempic and Mounjaro may have a surprising effect on your brain
articles.summary: Blockbuster weight loss drugs like Ozempic and Mounjaro may do more than help people shed pounds, with growing evidence suggesting they could also influence brain health. Although studies have linked GLP-1 medications to a lower risk of dementia, major trials found that semaglutide did not slow Alzheimer's disease. Scientists suspect these drugs may be more effective at preserving memory and thinking abilities in people with obesity or diabetes, especially before cognitive problems appear.

articles.title: Mindfulness therapy alters brain waves in major depressive disorder
articles.summary: Combining mindfulness therapy with standard antidepressant medication reduces depression symptoms while simultaneously altering the brain's electrical activity. A new study reveals how cognitive training shifts specific brain waves to help patients better regulate their emotions.

articles.title: Daily peanut consumption may improve brain insulin responsiveness in older adults
articles.summary: Eating two servings of unsalted, skin-roasted peanuts daily for 16 weeks may alter how memory-related brain areas respond to insulin in older adults, according to a randomized trial published in Food & Function.

articles.title: Human-AI Mutualism Is Unstable under Capability Asymmetry
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.23322v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: One hope for a good human future alongside advanced AI rests on enduring mutualism: humans and AI will need each other, so the relationship will stay good for both. We argue that this hope fails as AI capability grows. Bargaining guarantees each side only what it would get if bargaining failed. For humans, this can be less than they had before AI. articles.title: Training Language Models for Introspective Oversight
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.23365v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language models increasingly exhibit behaviors that are difficult to detect in transcripts, such as reward hacking, deception, and sycophancy. Asking the assistant follow-up questions about its actions is unreliable, since models are generally not trained to report their own misbehavior. As a result, approaches to oversight typically involve querying external models. articles.summary: arXiv:2611.23375v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coding agents are billed by the token, yet software engineering says nothing about what a token actually buys. articles.title: GridForge: An Open Physics-Informed Digital Twin and Benchmark Suite for UK 11 kV Underground Distribution Cables
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.23241v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The UK distribution-cable monitoring sector is data-rich but framework-poor: each Distribution Network Operator (DNO) collects megabytes of telemetry per asset per day, but there is no public benchmark dataset, no shared reference model, and no commonly agreed evaluation protocol for benchmarking sectoral, data-intensive models for operational decision support; notably for maintenance planning and prioritisation. We address this gap with GridForge, an open-source physics-informed digital twin and benchmark suite for fault diagnosis and prediction

articles.title: Is free will an illusion? New brain research reveals a surprising twist
articles.summary: New research reveals that the brain makes free choices and forced decisions using surprisingly similar neural processes, with activity building toward a decision before we act. The discovery challenges assumptions about free will while suggesting that our personal preferences and experiences still shape what we choose.
